article_title: An Individual Participant Data Meta-analysis of the Joint Effects of Social, Dimensional, and Temporal Comparisons on Students’ Academic Self-Concepts
citation: Fabian Wolff · Jens Möller. (2022). An Individual Participant Data Meta-analysis of the Joint Effects of Social, Dimensional, and Temporal Comparisons on Students' Academic Self-Concepts. Educational Psychology Review (2022) 34:2569–2608. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-022-09686-1
title: The 2I/E model: joint effects of social, dimensional, and temporal comparisons on academic self-concepts
description: The 2I/E model extends Marsh's classic internal/external frame of reference model by adding temporal comparisons as a second internal comparison. It "describes the effects of students' math and verbal achievements on their math and verbal self-concepts in a more differentiated fashion than the classic I/E model by considering achievement information from different points in time, and separating students' achievement levels from their achievement changes." It predicts positive within-subject effects of achievement levels and changes, negative between-subject level effects, and orders effect strength: social > dimensional > temporal. The meta-analysis tested it on pooled data from 10 datasets (N = 45,248).
requirements: Achievement and self-concept measures in two subjects (math and first language) at the beginning and end of a temporal comparison period, so achievement levels and achievement changes can be computed
constraints: The models are simplified representations that do not claim to capture all determinants of self-concept formation, and the regression approach does not allow causal conclusions
Dimensional comparisons are specified only between math and verbal achievements, and social comparisons refer to all other students examined in the study rather than local reference groups
target_learners: school students in math and first-language domains, grades 6–11
examples: The IPD meta-analysis regressed math self-concept on math achievement level, the math–verbal achievement-level difference, and math achievement change, and analogously for verbal self-concept, across 10 pooled datasets
